title: Verdict broker and audit-forwarder middleware for unified API/runtime/console
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: RBAC v2 introduces richer, attribute-aware policies that must be enforced consistently across three touchpoints: public API, internal runtime (inference request path), and the administrative Console. Current enforcement is fragmented: API-level gate checks are duplicated, runtime path uses a lightweight allowlist, and Console relies on coarse-grained backend flags. This ticket implements a unified 'verdict broker' — a small, low-latency policy evaluation adapter that returns a canonical decision plus explainability metadata — and an 'audit-forwarder' middleware that guarantees durable, structured audit events for every authorization decision. Goals: (1) Single canonical decision shape consumed by API gateways, runtime interceptors, and Console backend; (2) Deterministic audit events delivered to the audit pipeline (Kafka -> long-term store) with request correlation IDs; (3) Fast path (<1ms median added latency for common cachable checks) with safe slow-path for complex attribute checks; (4) Backwards-compatible rollout with canary and opt-out toggles. Scope: Implement verdict broker service + shared client lib; integrate middleware into API gateway, runtime request path, and Console auth layer; wire audit-forwarder to existing audit stream. Non-goals: Rewriting policy language or policy authoring UI (handled by separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Unified decision payload schema documented and approved (schema link in links)
API gateway and runtime use shared client to request decisions in >=95% of production requests in canary org
Audit-forwarder emits structured events for every evaluated request and persists to Kafka topic 'rbac-decisions' with 99.9% delivery observed in staging tests
End-to-end latency regression <1ms median for cached decisions; p95 <10ms in synthetic load tests
Feature flags exist to roll back to legacy checks per service and per org
Security review completed and signed-off by InfoSec with mitigation plan for any gaps
tasks: Design verdict payload and explanatory fields (reason, policy_id, matched_rules, confidence)
Implement lightweight verdict-broker service with Redis-backed decision cache and metrics
Publish client SDK (Go/TypeScript) with sync/async call options and local cache hooks
Add audit-forwarder middleware to API gateway: attach request metadata and forward to Kafka topic
Integrate runtime interceptor: call verdict broker before kv-cache lookup; respect allow/deny with fallback policies
Integrate Console backend: use verdict for UI access controls and surface explainability to admins (read-only)
Create feature flags and rollout plan (canary orgs -> region -> global)
Write load and reliability tests; run chaos tests simulating verdict-broker outage
Prepare runbook for failed audits and audit-forwarder retries
Coordinate SSO/SAML mapping changes with identity team to ensure subject attributes are available
decisions: Keep policy language (existing DSL) unchanged for this iteration; broker will evaluate via existing policy evaluator binary
Verdict schema will include a short canonical 'reason_code' to simplify downstream metrics and alerts
Audit-forwarder will be implemented as asynchronous best-effort with exactly-once semantic approximated via idempotent event keys
Use Redis for short-lived decision cache and Postgres for cold-store reference (no policy persistence in broker)
Expose explainability metadata to Console only when org-level setting 'show-policy-explain' is enabled
